comment: Professor Hoyle is probably the most dedicated person on campus to helping us learn. The content of the class is incredibly difficult and Hoyle does a great job of guiding us through it and making sure we understand. However, he can come off as rude and treats the class as a 2 unit one, as opposed to a 1 unit one.

Hoyle is by far the most challenging professor you will take at this school, and he is teaching probably the most challenging course. The class is a grind, and you will have to devote practically all your time to it. But, Hoyle is probably the most skilled and passionate professor I've ever had. If ur an accounting major, definitley take him.

Professor Hoyle was one of the most engaging and difficult professors I have ever had. The course is incredibly difficult, with your entire grade comprising of 4 tests. The content is challenging but informative and Hoyle is a great resource in office hours. While he can be a bit rude and his handwriting is illegible, he is still a great professor.

Professor Hoyle uses a socratic teaching style for his classes, and so you must be prepared for every class. Tests are graded moderately hard and they make up 100% of your grade. He is often available in his office and can help you with accounting questions. The worst part is that his handwriting is atrocious which is why I gave him 4 instead of 5.

If you are planning on majoring in accounting take Hoyle! You will learn so much more than any other professor that it is worth it being a little harder. If you put in the time to do the hw and extra problems you will do fine and it won't be that hard.
Amazing professor.
Great teacher

Hoyle is one of the best professor you could ever meet in this school. I would say I wasted my 300k tuition if I didn't meet him in this school. Go take him and challenge yourself. Do what he suggested you to do and talk with him. You will be fine in his class and acct would be interesting. You will learn a lot.
My most enjoyed class in UR. He is the kind of teacher that worth knowing and meeting for not only your major but also your life.

The hardest and best professor I've taken at UR. Working for the A will require you to put this class first above your others, but a B is more manageable. Prepare for class ahead of time and ask questions in office hours if you're confused (you will be). I would take Hoyle for all of my accounting classes if he taught them.

Hoyle is easy to love, easy to hate. His teaching philosophy is unlike anything I have ever encountered. SO much material to cover at breakneck pace. Some of the problems for homework or on exams are so outlandish that completing them feels like fighting a war. You really have to enjoy the material and the intense pace of the course to like him.

If you ever get the chance to take Hoyle's 201 please do so. I have never been more engaged in a class or proud of the work I did. You will have to put in the effort to learn but Hoyle gives you the resources so that learning is not overly complicated. If you do the daily sheets and take advantage of review sessions, an A is definitely achievable.

best prof ever. do the worksheets before class. do the guided reading cards. do everything he says. every practice problem. turn on ur email notifications bc he will send probably an email per day. you have to want an A. you cannot slack or miss class. u might not like him at first but probably the class u will learn the most in.

Prof. Hoyle is definitely the best teacher I have ever met. The course is not so hard unless you don't pay enough effort. He is always willing to solve any problems. I would strongly recommend you to take this fantastic course.

Hoyle is one of those professors that you will hate for the first half of the semester, but by the second half you will come to appreciate his teaching style. He expects a lot of his students, and it's easy to complain at first, but I have never learned so much from a class. It's definitely a marathon, not a sprint, but he will help you learn.

I would describe this as a marathon, but you're on fire. No homework is graded - based only on exams and one project. Hoyle is caring and his courses are forcefully engaging. He breaks you down and rebuilds your understanding of accounting. Most difficult class thus far but also the one in which I've learned the most. This class will make you cry.

If you want to learn the material, this is your guy. So much work, but so good. There are many different ways to learn built in, so there will be something that helps you specifically - readings, in-depth examples, practice problems, videos, etc. I had low stake quizzes 2x a week usually. They are low stress but really show what you need to work on

Hoyle is a hard professor but he really cares about his students. I was very intimidated when I started receiving emails from him many weeks before my classes had started but he really makes you work hard because he wants you to succeed. I found him happy to help when I was facing issues and the way he structures classes is super engaging

Professor Hoyle is hands down the best professor I've had at any stage of my life, and it's easy to see why he's a living legend at UR. The class itself has a reputation of being extremely hard, and Hoyle definitely challenges you, but it's one of the best experiences you'll have. Hoyle really cares for every student and makes accounting seem fun.

Professor Hoyle is a knowledgable professor, but his tests are not reflective of what is taught in class. The class examples are reasonably easy to understand and do, but the tests are nothing comparable. The tests feel like they were given by another teacher who was not teaching you. I did learn alot from him, but my test grades don't reflect it.

Hoyle is an interesting guy. He sends a million emails to the class over the semester which are a lot, but it's obvious that it's just because he cares so much. You will learn more about accounting from him than anyone else, but this also comes with high expectations and lots of homework/studying. If you're willing to put in the work, take him.

By far the best accounting professor, but also the hardest. He wrote the textbook that all the other accounting professors use, except you, get all his extra knowledge and assignments. He truly wants you to succeed and provides the steps to do so. It isn't easy but you'll learn the most if you're interested in accounting.

Best professor I've had, wrote textbook and all other materials associated with class. Significantly more difficult than the majority of profs, but you'll know more ab accounting than probably anyone else in virginia. special class, do everything he tells u to do (which is a LOT) and you will get at least a B, he knows better than any of us

VERY scary class; Hoyle calls on you at random so pay attention, do HW. BUT amazing class, learned a ton, enjoyed myself (when I wasn't super nervous) and did well. My main tip is to do EXACTLY what he says; it may seem silly but if you follow his advice then you will do well. Slacking off will guarantee a bad grade so be careful. Good luck!

Hoyle is an amazing teacher who some how makes accounting the most interesting thing in the world. But you're sole grades come from 4 tests the whole semester and the tests are hard. Even if you are prepared everyday don't expect an A because it only takes one bad test. Take him for the experience for sure if your GPA can afford it.

the way he structures this class is absolutely idiotic. he does not test in the same fashion he teaches. he lectures and drills you on vocab but then tests application. Imagine spending three-four weeks in a calculus class only DISCUSSING how to solve an integral but then on the test you are expected to integrate by parts.

Hands down the best professor in the B school. Hardest class you will every take but you will learn more than in any other class before. Best advice is to come to class prepared, go to office hours, and take his advice with meeting outside of class early with classmates to go over homework.

The best accounting professor in the business school, no debate. He's also arguably the most difficult. He definitely makes you work for it, but you learn so much along the way. If you're a prospective accounting major then I would 100% recommend taking him for 201. If you're unsure about majoring in business in general, then don't take his class.

Hoyle is THE best teacher that I have ever had. He not only teaches the material, but relates it to real business situations and helps you become more knowledgable about the business world. He has very high expectations but they are definitely not impossible to meet. Make a study group, go to every class prepared, take good notes during class.
He is a great professor. His class is inspiring. Tests are hard, and he absolutely wants you to work really hard. Will learn a lot in his class. HE WROTE THE TEXT BOOK.

best professor ever. Had him 201 last semester. He wants you to succeed. Do what he says. Do the handouts before class. Go to office hours. He makes accounting so fun and the class rewarding. Everyone in B school should take him whether or not they want to understand accounting.

Absolutely loved him as a professor, I know more about accounting than people in any of the other classes, but the tests were extremely difficult, and you have to be prepared to put in a lot of work outside of class. He's difficult, but if you're interested in Accounting, it's helpful because you learn so much.
Tests are the most important part of his class. Figure out his tricks and you can do well, it just takes work on your part

If you are willing to make his class your top priority in college and put in a ridiculous amount of work in order to learn as much as possible about accounting, take his class. Otherwise, steer clear and take another professor where you will still learn a good amount but with significantly less work.

Hoyle is an amazing teacher because he really cares about his students and he makes a boring subject interesting. The class is extremely tough--even when you think you understand something, he'll put tricks in the test he knows will trip up even the best students. You really never know how you do on the tests. TAKE GOOD NOTES AND PREPARE FOR CLASS!

The reviews are true he is a very hard teacher, you will learn accounting and if you want an A or even an average grade you’re going to have to try very hard. He is very passionate but teaches the class in a way where you basically teach yourself but it ends up working. He emails at least everyday and tests are 100% of your grade. He wrote the book

Hoyle is by far the best professor I have had.  I didn't work as hard as I should have in the class and I regret it. Just come to class prepared he calls on people randomly so do the homework or be ready to look stupid, I know I had to say I don't know multiple times. Just do the work and you will do great.
Most amazing professor I've had at Richmond. He is very tough, but you come out of the class really knowing the material
He is simply the best.  Take him if you want to learn the principles of accounting and a lot more beyond that!! =D

I got crushed in this class and got a C. But this is the best professor I have ever had. Learned a ton about accounting and life. I would take the gpa drop any day just to get the wisdom from this guy. Truly a pillar of the UR community and business world
Pretty difficult but Hoyle is a great guy! I would recommend him to anyone who has to take the class but is not overly enthusiastic about accounting.

Fantastic Professor! Some people say he is really difficult. Not true. But class preparation is key. And he stresses that as well. Do the readings and work on the handout and you'll do just fine. Definitely one of the best professors I've had a UR.
Best professor I had at UR

definitely take Hoyle's class.  He is great and you really learn a whole lot.  I started off taking it as a requirement to get into bschool but am now seriously considering majoring in accounting. Contrary to many, I don't find him difficult, as long as you do all the reading and lesson preparation, you will get a good grade.

Hoyle is the best teacher at UR hands down. He is tough though and pushes you. Students who get a "C" in his class probably learn more than those who get an "A" in another 201. If you want an easy "A", don't take Hoyle. But if you actually want to learn something and have a fantastic teacher, I strongly recommend Hoyle.

Take. This. Class. Hoyle is by far the best professor at UR. His classes are hard because he wants you to learn. He really cares about his students. You are called on randomly during class, and usually at least 2. Never less than 1. By the end of the semester, you will really learn everything he taught you.

Hoyle is the best teacher at UR! But his class is extremely difficult. You will learn more then you need to and often times class is very intimidating. The entire class is a discussion and you will talk at least 3 times per class. This class taught me to be prepared and confident. Hoyle is amazing!

Had Hoyle for Acct 201 and he's easily the best teacher I've had at Richmond. Very engaging and can get on a roll cracking jokes and stuff. He cares a lot about his students and has a ton of office hours. The textbook has everything you need to know because he wrote it. Just do the reading and you can definitely an A. Great prof

Notice all good comments about hoyle are from 300 level classes DO NOT TAKE FOR 201 will destroy your GPA and is too caught up with his 300 level classes to care that much about 201 every time you email him about a question he gives you a demeaning response pretends to care pretends to do half the work horrible prof for 201 bunch of ppl think so

Hoyle is a must take as a accounting major. Don't take him "for fun" though. He'll ruin your GPA if you don't make Accounting your life, but its well worth it for everything you learn. Its best to be prepared for class but most of the time you can follow the discussion, its just harder that way. He'll call on you at least once every class.

I am confident that taking this class is the most valuable academic experience I will ever have. By far the best professor at Richmond. Go see him after class, become his friend. Try not to get frustrated, you may study 15 hours for a test and get a C.  Attendance policy: If you don't go, you're screwed.

As everyone has said, Great Professor and forces you to learn the material.  I worked by far the hardest for this guy but also learned the most.  He loves to send out emails about life lessons but some are interesting.  Be ready for LOTS of work but lots of learning too.

Professor Hoyle is indeed the best professor in the business school. His tests are challenging but very fair.  If you have any interest in accounting or business in general, then you must take this class.  The curve is extremely helpful so making an A is reasonable while getting below a C is almost impossible.

Attendance is not mandatory, but this class is one that will kill you if you don't come to it.  It is an extremely difficult course, but interesting and worth the time. Hoyle is one of those profs you either love or hate, and is also one of those profs that you will remember your entire life.
Most challenging class I have ever taken hands down. However, Hoyle is the best professor in the bschool.
extremely thorough

A very good teacher. Makes class interesting. Goes around the room and has a conversation with students as a teaching method. If you prepare for class, you should do fine. Do not take him if you feel like slacking off though. Everyone says he is hard, including him, but he's really not if you put the effort in. Interesting guy.

The best professor ther is. He mekes you love the subject and if you don't learn it with him you will never do it. He is hard, but as long as you are prepare for class and ask questions you will do fine.

AMAZING professor...best at Richmond. Not easy, but if you work you can earn a good grade.  Always ready to help and explains material in a clear and easy to understand way.  Take him...especially if you are going to major in accounting.

Hoyle is probably one of the most effective teachers I will ever have. He explains comlplicated concepts in a way that everyone can understand. He truly cares and really pushes all of his students. HOWEVER, his tests are extremely challenging. Take Hoyle for the education and not for the grade.

Go in knowing you will have a lot of work but you will come out with so much background and great understanding.  He expects a lot but is person specific and will always be there to help you.  Great profession.  Absolutely love him!
Everyone loves Joe Ben
No Comments
Not the best professor, but good. Keeps your interest and puts pressure on you to know the material. Tests are a little tricky, will need to work hard to get about a B.
Easily the best professor, hands down. I would take as many possible classes from him.  Some say he is tough, but if you do the homework before class, he is down-right easy.
The best professor you will ever have.  Keeps you on your toes and drives you crazy, but you'll never believe how much info he manages to cram into your brain.

Hoyle is a great teacher. He doesn't mince words - says what's on his mind (one of the "don't wear a hat to my class" kind of profs). Rumor has it that this guy doesn't pass his CPA each year on purpose so he knows what the test looks like from year to year. Take his class! He's accounting incarnate
awesome intro class
Amazing Professor!! Must take if your planning on CPA.
No Comments
He demands a lot from you, but you'll get a lot out of the class.

Hoyle ROCKS.
